content: Dr. Robert Coleman Atkins, born on October 17, 1930, and passing on April 17, 2003, was an American physician and cardiologist. He is most renowned for developing the Atkins Nutritional Approach, commonly referred to as the Atkins Diet. This dietary regimen emphasizes the consumption of low-carbohydrate, high-protein foods, along with leafy vegetables and dietary supplements. While popular, the diet has also been a subject of significant controversy. Dr. Atkins completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Michigan in 1951 and earned his medical degree from Cornell Medical College in 1955. He subsequently specialized in cardiology and complementary medicine. Around the year 2000, Dr. Atkins developed a heart condition known as cardiomyopathy, which he asserted was unrelated to his dietary practices. On April 18, 2002, he experienced cardiac arrest. On April 8, 2003, he suffered a severe fall on ice outside his medical office in New York City, resulting in major head injuries that left him in a coma. This incident led to widespread rumors that he had suffered a heart attack while following his own diet. However, these claims were unfounded. Dr. Atkins never recovered from his injuries and ultimately passed away on April 17, 2003, due to kidney failure. Following his death, the New York City Medical Examiner’s Office mistakenly released his medical records to the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, a group associated with PETA that advocates for vegetarian diets. These records indicated that Dr. Atkins weighed approximately 255 pounds (116 kg) at the time of his death, which classified him as obese based on BMI calculations. This information was widely disseminated by the media and animal rights groups, leading to public scrutiny and distress for his family. The Atkins company later clarified that his weight upon hospital admission was 196 pounds (89 kg) and that the apparent weight gain was due to fluid retention caused by organ failure. Journalist William Leith, who interviewed Dr. Atkins between his cardiac arrest and his fall, described him as being just under six feet tall and weighing around 200 pounds. Leith noted that Dr. Atkins did not appear overweight, with minimal signs of excess weight around his neck, attributing his appearance to age rather than obesity. On July 31, 2005, Atkins Nutritionals, the company founded by Dr. Atkins in 1989, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York. The company had faced financial difficulties due to the declining popularity of the Atkins Diet and the rise of competing high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet plans. By January 10, 2006, the company emerged from bankruptcy with a revised business strategy that shifted focus away from the low-carbohydrate diet and toward the sale of prepared nutritional bars and shakes. Dr. Atkins authored numerous books throughout his career, many of which became bestsellers. These include The Essential Atkins for Life Kit (2003), Dr. Atkins' Diet Planner (2003), Atkins for Life: The Next Level (2003), Dr. Atkins' New Diet Revolution (2002), Dr. Atkins' Age-Defying Diet (2001), Dr. Atkins' Vita-Nutrient Solution (1997), Dr. Atkins' Quick & Easy New Diet Cookbook (1997), Dr. Atkins' New Carbohydrate Gram Counter (1996), Dr. Atkins' New Diet Cookbook (1994), Dr. Atkins' Health Revolution (1988), Dr. Atkins' Nutrition Breakthrough (1981), Dr. Atkins' Super Energy Diet Cookbook (1978), and Dr. Atkins' Super Energy Diet (1978). His works have had a lasting impact on the field of nutrition and dietetics.
